title: Using Bad Learners to find Good Configurations

edges.target: Projective sampling (Sarkar et al., ASE'15)
edges.ref: [18] A. Sarkar, J. Guo, N. Siegmund, S. Apel, K. Czarnecki. 2015. Cost-Efficient Sampling for Performance Prediction of Configurable Systems. ASE, 342-352.
edges.evidence: We measure the benefit of our rank-based approach as the percentage of required measurements needed by state-of-the-art techniques in this field (see Sarkar et al. [18] presented at ASE'15).

edges.target: Progressive sampling (residual-based, as described by Sarkar et al.)
edges.ref: [18] A. Sarkar, J. Guo, N. Siegmund, S. Apel, K. Czarnecki. 2015. Cost-Efficient Sampling for Performance Prediction of Configurable Systems. ASE, 342-352.
edges.evidence: we discuss the residual-based approaches for building performance models ... For further details, we refer to Sarkar et. al [18]. ... progressive and projective sampling, respectively.

edges.target: CART performance prediction (Guo et al., ASE'13)
edges.ref: [5] J. Guo, K. Czarnecki, S. Apel, N. Siegmund, A. Wasowski. 2013. Variability-Aware Performance Prediction: A Statistical Learning Approach. ASE, 301-311.
edges.evidence: when the state-of-the-art technique of Guo at al. [5] is applied to these software systems, the error rates of the generated predictor is up to 80%

edges.target: Apache Storm configuration datasets (Jamshidi & Casale)
edges.ref: [7] P. Jamshidi and G. Casale. 2016. An Uncertainty-Aware Approach to Optimal Configuration of Stream Processing Systems. MASCOTS, 39-48.
edges.evidence: we also consider Apache Storm, a distributed system, in several scenarios. The datasets were obtained from the paper by Jamshidi et al. [7].

edges.target: Configurable-system performance datasets SS1-SS8 (x264, BerkeleyDB, SQLite, wget, lrzip, Dune, HSMGP, Apache; SPLConqueror lineage)
edges.ref: [21] N. Siegmund, S. S. Kolesnikov, C. Kaestner, S. Apel, D. Batory, M. Rosenmueller, G. Saake. 2012. Predicting Performance via Automated Feature-Interaction Detection. ICSE.
edges.evidence: we evaluate it using 21 test cases collected in 9 open-source software systems. For more details on the subject systems and configurations options refer to http://tiny.cc/3wpwly

edges.target: scikit-learn (CART implementation)
edges.ref: [16] F. Pedregosa et al. 2011. Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python. JMLR 12, 2825-2830.
edges.evidence: we took care to either clearly define our algorithms or use implementations from the public domain (scikit-learn) [16].

edges.target: Non-parametric bootstrap test (Efron & Tibshirani)
edges.ref: [2] B. Efron and R. J. Tibshirani. 1993. An Introduction to the Bootstrap. CRC.
edges.evidence: For testing statistical significance, we used a non-parametric bootstrap test with 95% confidence [2]

edges.target: A12 effect size (Vargha & Delaney)
edges.ref: [22] A. Vargha and H. D. Delaney. 2000. A Critique and Improvement of the CL Common Language Effect Size Statistics of McGraw and Wong. JEBS 25, 101-132.
edges.evidence: followed by an A12 test to check that any observed differences were not trivially small effects ... (as per Vargha [22], we say that a small effect has a < 0.6)

edges.target: Scott-Knott ranking (Mittas & Angelis)
edges.ref: [12] N. Mittas and L. Angelis. 2013. Ranking and Clustering Software Cost Estimation Models through a Multiple Comparisons Algorithm. TSE 39, 537-551.
edges.evidence: we use the Scott-Knott test to recursively divide our approaches ... This use of the Scott-Knott test is endorsed by Mittas and Angelis [12]

edges.target: Scott-Knott for classifier comparison (Ghotra, McIntosh, Hassan)
edges.ref: [4] B. Ghotra, S. McIntosh, A. E. Hassan. 2015. Revisiting the Impact of Classification Techniques on the Performance of Defect Prediction Models. ICSE, 789-800.
edges.evidence: This use of the Scott-Knott test is endorsed by Mittas and Angelis [12] and by Hassan et al. [4].

edges.target: MMRE residual accuracy metric (as used by Sarkar et al. / Guo et al.)
edges.ref: [18] A. Sarkar, J. Guo, N. Siegmund, S. Apel, K. Czarnecki. 2015. Cost-Efficient Sampling for Performance Prediction of Configurable Systems. ASE, 342-352.
edges.evidence: The accuracy of the models is calculated using MMRE (from Equation 2). ... instead of using residual measures of errors ... we use a rank-based measure.

edges.target: 'Lives' convergence/termination criterion (GALE, Krall et al.)
edges.ref: [9] J. Krall, T. Menzies, M. Davies. 2015. GALE: Geometric Active Learning for Search-Based Software Engineering. TSE 41, 1001-1018.
edges.evidence: then a life is lost. This termination criterion is widely used in the field of multi-objective optimization to determine degree of convergence [9].

edges.target: Validity/reliability definitions (Siegmund, Siegmund & Apel)
edges.ref: [20] J. Siegmund, N. Siegmund, S. Apel. 2015. Views on Internal and External Validity in Empirical Software Engineering. ICSE, 9-19.
edges.evidence: Validity refers to the extent to which a piece of research actually investigates what the researcher purports to investigate [20].

edges.target: Prior <5% MMRE predictors via sub-sampling (Nair et al., spectral learning)
edges.ref: [15] V. Nair, T. Menzies, N. Siegmund, S. Apel. 2017. Faster Discovery of Faster System Configurations with Spectral Learning. arXiv.
edges.evidence: prior work [15] has used sub-sampling to build predictors for configuration runtimes using predictors with error rates less than 5%

edges.target: Developers ignore over 83% of configuration options (Xu et al.)
edges.ref: [24] T. Xu, L. Jin, X. Fan, Y. Zhou, S. Pasupathy, R. Talwadker. 2015. Hey, You Have Given Me Too Many Knobs! ESEC/FSE, 307-319.
edges.evidence: developers tend to ignore over 83% of configuration options, which leaves considerable optimization potential untapped and induces major economic cost [24].

edges.target: Accurate models need hundreds of measurements (Siegmund et al. ICSE'12 / Guo / Sarkar)
edges.ref: [21] N. Siegmund, S. S. Kolesnikov, C. Kaestner, S. Apel, D. Batory, M. Rosenmueller, G. Saake. 2012. Predicting Performance via Automated Feature-Interaction Detection. ICSE.
edges.evidence: Such accurate models require the evaluation/measurement of hundreds of configuration options for training [5, 18, 21].

edges.target: MMRE causes conclusion instability (Foss et al.; Myrtveit & Stensrud; Myrtveit, Stensrud & Shepperd)
edges.ref: [3] T. Foss, E. Stensrud, B. Kitchenham, I. Myrtveit. 2003. A Simulation Study of the Model Evaluation Criterion MMRE. TSE 29, 985-995.
edges.evidence: MMRE along with other accuracy statistics such as MMRE, MBRE has been shown to cause conclusion instability [3, 13, 14].

edges.target: Ranking robust to errors/outliers (Rosset et al.; Kloke & McKean Rfit)
edges.ref: [17] S. Rosset, C. Perlich, B. Zadrozny. 2005. Ranking-based Evaluation of Regression Models. ICDM.
edges.evidence: Ranking is extremely robust since it is only mildly affected by errors or outliers [8, 17].

edges.target: Surrogate approximation error can help search (Lim et al.)
edges.ref: [10] D. Lim, Y. Jin, Y. S. Ong, B. Sendhoff. 2010. Generalizing Surrogate-Assisted Evolutionary Computation. IEEE TEVC 14, 329-355.
edges.evidence: A model capable to smoothing the complex landscape of a problem can be beneficial for the search process. This sentiment has been echoed in the evolutionary algorithm literature as well [10].

edges.target: Acquiring optimal configuration is expensive (Weiss & Tian)
edges.ref: [23] G. M. Weiss and Y. Tian. 2008. Maximizing Classifier Utility when there are Data Acquisition and Modeling Costs. DMKD, 253-282.
edges.evidence: Other researchers have commented that, in real-world scenarios, the cost of acquiring the optimal configuration is overly expensive and time-consuming [23].

edges.target: Measurement bias can cause false interpretations (Menzies et al., local vs global)
edges.ref: [11] T. Menzies, A. Butcher, D. Cok, A. Marcus, L. Layman, F. Shull, B. Turhan, T. Zimmermann. 2013. Local versus Global Lessons for Defect Prediction and Effort Estimation. TSE 39.
edges.evidence: We are aware that this evaluation leaves room for outliers and that measurement bias can cause false interpretations [11].

not_reuse_examples: [1] Chen et al. 2016 'Is Sampling better than Evolution' and [19] Sayyad et al. 2013 - cited only as background on functional-property configuration optimization; not run or compared.
[6] Henard et al. 2015 - background mention of SAT solver + MOEA product-line configuration; not reused.
GitHub ai-se/Reimplement reproduction package - the paper's own artifact, not prior work.
notes: Empirical SE paper (rank-based vs residual-based sampling for configuration optimization, 21 scenarios/9 systems); text cites 'Arcuri and Briand at ICSE'11 [12]' but [12] is Mittas & Angelis (mis-citation); origin of SS1-SS8 datasets only given via tiny.cc link, so that dataset edge is low confidence.
